problem.title: Why design intelligence matters for AI coding
problem.lead: Modern AI assistants are great at writing component code, but UI design taste is uneven. Without grounding, models tend to produce the same handful of layouts and color schemes across very different products. A medical dashboard ends up looking like a crypto app; a children's app uses fintech-grey. UI UX Pro Max Skill exists to fix that gap by pinning the model's choices to evidence-based, industry-aware design knowledge.

points.title: Generic patterns
points.body: Without context, models default to a centered hero, three feature cards, and a CTA. The skill exposes [[landing]] landing patterns and [[styles]] visual styles so the model has real choices to reason about for each project.

points.title: No industry context
points.body: A fintech dashboard and a wellness app have completely different color, density, and motion requirements. [[reasoning]] industry-specific reasoning rules let the model pick palettes and patterns that feel native to the domain.

points.title: Hidden anti-patterns
points.body: AI assistants happily generate code with poor contrast ratios, illegible font sizes, or interaction patterns that fail on mobile. The skill bundles [[ux]] UX guidelines and explicit anti-pattern lists so the model knows what to avoid.

architecture.title: How it works at a glance
architecture.body: The upstream Python generator searches bundled product, style, palette, landing and typography data, then combines recommendations using industry rules. The AI assistant separately uses that output to implement an interface. Runtime varies with the query and environment. The bundled Python search runs locally. Your AI assistant may send prompts, files and search output to its provider; its own privacy settings apply. CLI installation and update checks can use the network.

features.title: What's Included
features.intro: Every number below is a separately curated dataset that the reasoning engine can search and combine. Together they give the model enough raw material to produce design systems that feel hand-crafted instead of templated.

items.title: [[styles]] UI Styles

comparison.title: How it compares to alternatives
comparison.subtitle: There are several ways to bring design taste into your AI workflow. Here is where each one fits.

rows.strengths: Zero setup. Works in any assistant. Maximum flexibility for one-off experiments.
rows.limits: Output drifts session to session. No industry reasoning. Anti-patterns slip through. You re-explain your taste every time.

rows.strengths: Strong visual fidelity. Good for handing off to humans.
rows.limits: A separate design-to-code workflow is needed; available integrations depend on the assistant and tooling.

rows.strengths: Codify colors, spacing, and typography. Survive across sessions when checked into the repo.
rows.limits: Only cover surface tokens. No guidance on layout, density, motion, or which style to use in the first place.

rows.strengths: Production-ready primitives. Solve the implementation layer well.
rows.limits: Style-agnostic by design. You still need to decide colors, typography, and patterns per product.

rows.strengths: Lives in your AI client. Combines style, palette, typography, patterns, and reasoning. Plays well with shadcn/ui and design tokens. Persistable per project.
rows.limits: Tuned for web and app interfaces; not a print or motion-graphics tool. Best paired with a component library, not a replacement for one.

primer.title: What is a design system, in this context?
primer.lead: A design system here is not a 500-page Figma library. It is a compact, machine-readable bundle of decisions: which layout pattern to use, which color palette, which typography pairing, which motion vocabulary, which interactions to favor, and which anti-patterns to avoid. The generator produces one of these bundles per request, tailored to your product type and intent.

items.title: Pattern
items.body: The structural choice — for example 'bento grid with sticky navigation', 'data-dense admin layout', or 'mobile-first card stack'. Drawn from [[landing]] landing and product patterns.

items.title: Style
items.body: Normal recommendations use [[activeStyles]] active styles. [[supplementalStyles]] supplemental styles serve explicit variant requests; [[deprecatedStyles]] deprecated entries are excluded from normal ranking. Landing patterns are a separate dataset.

items.title: Color & typography
items.body: The upstream palettes provide product-oriented color suggestions. Verify contrast and define light/dark semantic tokens in your implementation; not every entry contains a complete pair of themes. The upstream catalog pairs heading and body fonts with usage notes and font links. Check script coverage, font licensing and rendering for the languages you support.

items.title: Effects, motion & micro-interactions
items.body: Shadow scale, blur, gradient direction, hover transitions, page transitions, and reduced-motion fallbacks.

items.title: Anti-patterns
items.body: Things to explicitly avoid for this product type — e.g. high-saturation reds in healthcare, novelty fonts in fintech, slow modal cascades in admin tools.

steps.title: User Request

steps.title: Multi-Domain Search

steps.title: Reasoning Engine
steps.desc: Industry rules help select patterns, style priorities and related recommendations. Anti-patterns are guidance to review; they do not automatically prove that generated code is correct or accessible.

steps.title: Design System Output
steps.desc: Return pattern, style, colors, typography, effects, anti-patterns, and a pre-delivery checklist. The AI assistant uses this as the source of truth while writing your components.

deepDive.title: What each stage actually does
deepDive.subtitle: If you are curious about the internals, here is the long version.

stages.label: Stage 1 — Parsing the request
stages.body: The query is used to find product candidates and matching industry rules. Include the product, page and constraints rather than relying on vague adjectives.

stages.label: Stage 2 — Catalog search
stages.body: The Python code searches the bundled CSV catalogs with BM25-based ranking. This is a local retrieval step, not a web search or a promise of parallel execution.

stages.label: Stage 3 — Reasoning and conflict resolution
stages.body: Industry rules help select patterns, style priorities and related recommendations. Anti-patterns are guidance to review; they do not automatically prove that generated code is correct or accessible.

stages.label: Stage 4 — Assembling the output
stages.body: Design-system output defaults to ASCII. Use -f markdown for Markdown or --json for JSON. These are recommendations to review, not a guarantee that generated interfaces meet accessibility requirements.

anatomy.body: Illustrative learning examples, not recorded generator output or verified production results. Review contrast, layout and interaction behavior in your own project.
anatomy.exampleCode:
# Design System

Product type: SaaS analytics dashboard
Industry: B2B fintech
Illustrative example (not a captured run)

## Pattern
Dense data layout — sticky sidebar, 12-column grid, sticky table headers.
Reference: landing/data-dashboard-sticky-sidebar

## Style
Minimalism with subtle glass accents on hover cards.
Why: fintech anti-pattern bans high-saturation hero gradients;
minimalism + restrained glass keeps it credible.

## Colors
Primary:   #2563EB  (blue-600)
Surface:   #FFFFFF / #0B1220
Text:      #0F172A / #E2E8F0
Accent:    #10B981  (emerald, use sparingly for KPI deltas)
Check contrast in the implemented interface.

## Typography
Display: Inter 700 / 48-56 px
Body:    Inter 400 / 15-16 px / 1.55 line-height
Numeric: IBM Plex Mono for tabular figures

## Effects
Shadow scale: 0/1/2/4 only. Avoid deep shadows.
Motion:      150-200ms ease-out. Honor prefers-reduced-motion.

## Anti-patterns to avoid
- Don't use red as a brand color (signals loss)
- Don't auto-rotate carousels on the dashboard
- Don't hide bulk actions behind hover-only UI

## Pre-delivery checklist
- [ ] All chart colors are colorblind-safe
- [ ] Tabular numbers use mono font
- [ ] Empty states have illustrations and CTA
- [ ] Loading states show skeletons, not spinners-only

persist.title: Persist Design System
persist.body: --persist writes design-system/<project-slug>/MASTER.md under --output-dir (the current directory by default). Existing MASTER.md is preserved unless --force is used. Ask your assistant to read this file and the relevant page override; saving a file does not guarantee that every assistant loads it automatically.

scopes.title: Project-level vs page-level scope
scopes.body: With --persist -p "Acme" --page pricing, the page file is design-system/acme/pages/pricing.md. The existing master is retained. Tell the assistant to apply page rules over the master for that page; review generated overrides before use.

tuning.title: Tuning the output
tuning.subtitle: Use --variance, --motion and --density (1–10) with --design-system to adjust recommendations. To retheme an existing app, first inspect framework versions and existing semantic tokens; ask the assistant to change small component groups and verify each supported theme.

items.title: Add explicit style keywords
items.body: Append words like 'glassmorphism', 'brutalist', 'bento grid', or 'aurora' to your prompt. These bias the style search toward your preferred direction without overriding other domain rules.

items.title: Name the industry
items.body: 'Healthcare', 'fintech', 'e-commerce', 'wellness', or 'gaming' anchor the reasoning rules. The more specific the industry, the more confident the anti-pattern filtering.

items.title: Specify the surface
items.body: 'Landing page', 'dashboard', 'mobile screen', 'pricing page', 'settings page' — surface keywords pick the right landing-pattern subset and density level.

items.title: Re-run with --page for one-offs
items.body: With --persist -p "Acme" --page pricing, the page file is design-system/acme/pages/pricing.md. The existing master is retained. Tell the assistant to apply page rules over the master for that page; review generated overrides before use.

step3.title: Install skill for your AI assistant

manualInstall.description: This method requires a preparation computer with Node.js, npm and package access. The destination needs Python 3 and the chosen AI assistant, but does not need npm. The directory table below is a reference, not a downloadable installation.

steps.text: On the preparation computer, create and enter a new empty temporary folder. Run the pinned command below to generate a project-local Claude Code skill.

Copy the entire generated .claude/skills/ui-ux-pro-max/ directory, including SKILL.md, data/ and scripts/, to the same relative path in the destination project. Include hidden directories when transferring files. Back up an existing installation before replacing it.

In the destination project root, run the Python command below (use python instead of python3 on Windows if appropriate). Then open the project in Claude Code and explicitly ask it to use UI UX Pro Max. A successful search checks the copied data and scripts; it does not prove the assistant has loaded the skill.

manualInstall.otherAssistants: For another assistant, use its --ai value from the CLI list in a separate empty folder and transfer all generated files at their original relative paths. Some platforms also generate command or workflow files. Check that assistant’s skill-loading instructions; the paths below cover only the listed platforms.

prerequisites.description: The search script requires Python 3.x environment support.

decision.title: Choosing the right install method
decision.subtitle: Three options, each with a clear sweet spot.

options.title: CLI install (recommended)
options.when: You have npm and want updates handled automatically.
options.why: In CLI 2.15.0, uipro update checks GitHub releases. A different version triggers a CLI upgrade attempt, then asks you to rerun uipro init --ai <assistant> --force. At the same version it refreshes bundled skill files. Review local skill edits before overwriting; --global selects the global installation.

options.title: Copy a generated skill (Claude Code example)
options.when: Your destination has no npm, but another computer can prepare the skill, or you want to vendor a generated installation.
options.why: Generate with the pinned CLI on the preparation computer, then transfer the complete installation. Updates require repeating those steps and reviewing local changes.

options.title: Offline install
options.when: You are behind a strict firewall or working on a flight without GitHub access.
options.why: CLI 2.15.0 installs from bundled templates by default. --offline is a compatibility flag, not a version pin. To reproduce an installation, pin the npm package version. Obtaining the package and checking releases still require network access unless separately cached.

items.body: Check Python 3 and Node.js yourself. If missing, install them from their official distributions or your package manager. Do not assume macOS includes Python 3.

Install Python 3 from python.org and tick 'Add Python to PATH' during setup. Use PowerShell or Windows Terminal for the npm and python3 commands. If python3 is not recognized, try py -3 --version. WSL2 works exactly like the Linux instructions below if you prefer a Unix shell.

Most distributions already have Python 3. Install Node via your package manager (apt install nodejs npm on Debian/Ubuntu, dnf install nodejs on Fedora). For the latest Node, fnm or nvm is recommended over distribution packages, which often lag.

updates.title: Updating and version pinning
updates.body: In CLI 2.15.0, uipro update checks GitHub releases. A different version triggers a CLI upgrade attempt, then asks you to rerun uipro init --ai <assistant> --force. At the same version it refreshes bundled skill files. Review local skill edits before overwriting; --global selects the global installation.
updates.commands:
npm view ui-ux-pro-max-cli versions --json
uipro update --ai claude
uipro init --ai claude --force

uninstall.title: Uninstall and cleanup
uninstall.body: The first commands remove project/global skill files. npm uninstall removes the CLI package. Keep your design-system directory; it contains your design decisions.
uninstall.commands:
uipro uninstall --ai claude
uipro uninstall --ai claude --global
npm uninstall -g ui-ux-pro-max-cli

rows.cause: npm global bin is not on PATH, or you installed without -g.
rows.fix: Run npm config get prefix to find the global bin path and add it to PATH, or reinstall with npm install -g ui-ux-pro-max-cli.

rows.cause: Global npm install attempting to write to a system-owned directory.
rows.fix: Prefer a Node version manager (fnm, nvm) so node lives under your user. Avoid sudo npm install -g, which causes more problems than it solves.

rows.cause: Python 3 is not installed or not on PATH (common on Windows out of the box).
rows.fix: macOS: brew install python3. Windows: install from python.org with 'Add to PATH'. Linux: use the distro package manager.

anatomy.title: Anatomy of a great prompt
anatomy.lead: A weak prompt produces a generic result; a structured prompt produces a tailored one. Four signals do most of the work — include any three and the output quality jumps significantly.

parts.label: 1. Product type
parts.body: What kind of product is this? SaaS, e-commerce, healthcare app, fintech tool, portfolio, blog, mobile-first marketplace. This drives industry rules and color mood.

parts.label: 2. Surface
parts.body: Which page or screen? Landing page, dashboard, settings page, mobile checkout, pricing page, blog post template. Surface picks the right pattern subset and density.

parts.label: 3. Style hint (optional)
parts.body: Glassmorphism, brutalist, bento grid, minimalist, aurora, dark mode. Skip if you have no preference — the engine will pick a sensible default.

parts.label: 4. Constraints (optional)
parts.body: Accessibility level (WCAG AA, AAA), framework (Next.js + shadcn/ui), brand colors, mobile-first, or 'must work without JavaScript'.

worked.title: End-to-end worked examples
worked.subtitle: Illustrative learning examples, not recorded generator output or verified production results. Review contrast, layout and interaction behavior in your own project.

items.title: SaaS analytics dashboard
items.prompt: Build a SaaS analytics dashboard for a B2B fintech product. Dense tables, dark mode by default, must hit WCAG AA, stack is Next.js + shadcn/ui.
items.output:
Pattern: dense data layout, sticky sidebar, 12-col grid
Style: minimalism with subtle glass on hover cards
Palette: cool blue + emerald accent (#2563EB / #10B981)
Type:   Inter 400/600/700 + IBM Plex Mono for numerics
Effects: shadow scale 0/1/2/4, 150-200ms ease-out
Avoid:  red as brand color, auto-rotating carousels, hover-only bulk actions
Checklist: colorblind-safe charts, mono tabular figures, skeleton loading

items.title: Healthcare patient portal
items.prompt: Design a patient portal for a hospital system. Reassuring tone, large touch targets, multilingual ready, must avoid medical-error anti-patterns.
items.output:
Pattern: card-based information hierarchy with persistent quick-actions
Style: minimalism, low saturation, no novelty effects
Palette: muted teal + warm neutrals (#0E7C7B / #F5F1E8)
Type:   Source Sans Pro 400/600, generous line-height (1.7)
Effects: minimal shadows, no parallax, prefers-reduced-motion enforced
Avoid:  red as default error color (suggests harm), red+green pairing,
        dense data tables on landing surfaces
Checklist: WCAG AAA where possible, 44px+ touch targets, RTL-ready

items.title: Indie portfolio with dark mode
items.prompt: Personal portfolio site for a creative developer. Strong visual identity, glassmorphism vibe, dark mode default with light fallback.
items.output:
Pattern: scroll-driven case studies with sticky project nav
Style: glassmorphism + aurora gradient backgrounds
Palette: deep indigo + violet aurora (#1E1B4B / #7C3AED / #06B6D4)
Type:   Sora 600/800 display + Inter 400 body
Effects: backdrop-blur 12px, soft glow on hover, 400ms cubic ease-in-out
Avoid:  heavy noise textures, overlapping marquee text, motion-only nav
Checklist: respects prefers-reduced-motion, light-mode parity, image alt text

items.title: E-commerce mobile checkout
items.prompt: Mobile checkout flow for an apparel store. Three steps maximum, Apple Pay first, must work on slow 4G.
items.output:
Pattern: full-screen step pages, persistent total bar, no modal stacks
Style: flat 2.0 with strong typography, minimal decoration
Palette: warm off-white + brand accent + green for success states
Type:   System fonts for speed (San Francisco / Roboto), 16px+ body
Effects: instant transitions, skeleton placeholders, no carousel
Avoid:  third-party scripts on checkout, sticky promos that obscure CTA,
        forced account creation before payment
Checklist: payment-request API tested, address autofill, error recovery

items.title: Open-source docs site
items.prompt: Documentation site for an open-source library. Sidebar + search + content + on-this-page TOC. Clean, fast, dark mode toggle.
items.output:
Pattern: three-column docs (sidebar + content + TOC), sticky header
Style: minimalism, generous whitespace, monospace code blocks
Palette: neutral grays + single brand accent (no rainbow)
Type:   Inter 400/600 + JetBrains Mono for code
Effects: subtle hover states only, no animation on scroll

antiPrompts.title: Prompts that produce weak output
antiPrompts.lead: These patterns systematically miss the signals the generator needs. Avoid them.

items.why: No product type, no surface, no constraints. The model has nothing to ground on and falls back to a generic landing template.
No reference for 'better'. Better than what? In which direction? Specify a style hint or a concrete dimension to change.

items.bad: Build a beautiful, modern, clean, professional dashboard.
items.why: Adjective soup. None of those words narrow the search. Replace with industry, surface, and one concrete style keyword.
'Latest' is ambiguous and dates badly. Name the specific style (bento grid, glassmorphism) if that is what you want.

faq.overview: For translation or website errors, use the site feedback link below. For skill or CLI defects, use the upstream project link. This site does not provide official product support.

items.q: Which AI assistants are supported?
items.a: CLI 2.15.0: claude, cursor, windsurf, antigravity, copilot, kiro, codex, qoder, roocode, gemini, trae, opencode, continue, codebuddy, droid, kilocode, warp, augment, codewhale, universal. Use --ai all to generate all supported platform installations, not only detected assistants.

items.q: Do I need Node.js to use the skill itself?
items.a: No. The skill runs through Python at request time. You only need Node.js if you install via ui-ux-pro-max-cli (npm). The manual-install path requires nothing beyond Python 3.

items.q: Why Python 3? Can it run on Python 2?
items.a: Python 3 only. The search script uses f-strings, type hints, and modern dict ordering that do not exist in Python 2. Python 2 also reached end-of-life in 2020 and is no longer security-supported.

items.q: Where is search.py located?
items.a: Use the generated platform-specific installation. Claude: .claude/skills/ui-ux-pro-max/; Cursor: .cursor/skills/ui-ux-pro-max/; Windsurf: .windsurf/skills/ui-ux-pro-max/; Antigravity and Codex: .agents/skills/ui-ux-pro-max/. search.py is in scripts/ under each skill directory. Paths here apply to CLI 2.15.0.

items.q: Can I install without GitHub access?
items.a: CLI 2.15.0 installs from bundled templates by default. --offline is a compatibility flag, not a version pin. To reproduce an installation, pin the npm package version. Obtaining the package and checking releases still require network access unless separately cached.

items.q: Can I install the skill globally rather than per project?
items.a: Both project and global skill installs are supported. Example: uipro init --ai claude --global writes under ~/.claude/skills/. Installing the CLI with npm -g and installing a skill with --global are separate operations.

items.q: Do I need to specify a stack?
items.a: In CLI 2.15.0, run stack search separately: python3 .claude/skills/ui-ux-pro-max/scripts/search.py "forms accessibility" --stack shadcn. The --design-system branch takes precedence over --stack; combining them does not apply a stack filter to generation. Give both outputs to the assistant.

items.q: Which output formats are available?
items.a: Design-system output defaults to ASCII. Use -f markdown for Markdown or --json for JSON. These are recommendations to review, not a guarantee that generated interfaces meet accessibility requirements.

items.q: How does the model decide which industry I am in?
items.a: The upstream Python generator searches bundled product, style, palette, landing and typography data, then combines recommendations using industry rules. The AI assistant separately uses that output to implement an interface. Runtime varies with the query and environment.

items.q: How do I preserve brand decisions?
items.a: --persist writes design-system/<project-slug>/MASTER.md under --output-dir (the current directory by default). Existing MASTER.md is preserved unless --force is used. Ask your assistant to read this file and the relevant page override; saving a file does not guarantee that every assistant loads it automatically.

items.q: Can I generate just a single page's design without affecting the rest?
items.a: With --persist -p "Acme" --page pricing, the page file is design-system/acme/pages/pricing.md. The existing master is retained. Tell the assistant to apply page rules over the master for that page; review generated overrides before use.

items.q: The output is missing my favorite style. Can I add one?
items.a: Not yet through a public API. You can edit the CSV catalog under data/styles.csv after a local install if you want to extend it for your own use. Upstream contributions are welcome via the project repo.

items.q: Can I change the anti-pattern list for a given industry?
items.a: --persist writes design-system/<project-slug>/MASTER.md under --output-dir (the current directory by default). Existing MASTER.md is preserved unless --force is used. Ask your assistant to read this file and the relevant page override; saving a file does not guarantee that every assistant loads it automatically.

items.q: How do I get the model to use shadcn/ui by default?
items.a: In CLI 2.15.0, run stack search separately: python3 .claude/skills/ui-ux-pro-max/scripts/search.py "forms accessibility" --stack shadcn. The --design-system branch takes precedence over --stack; combining them does not apply a stack filter to generation. Give both outputs to the assistant.

items.q: Does the skill send anything to an external server?
items.a: The bundled Python search runs locally. Your AI assistant may send prompts, files and search output to its provider; its own privacy settings apply. CLI installation and update checks can use the network.

items.q: Is the skill free?
items.a: Yes, the skill itself is free and open source. You still pay for whatever AI assistant you use it with (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) under their normal pricing.

items.q: Does using the skill increase my AI token usage?
items.a: Search results add context tokens. Actual usage and fees depend on your assistant, model and task; fewer correction turns are not guaranteed.

items.q: How often does the skill get updated?
items.a: Upstream authors decide release timing. Check the linked release notes; this translation site does not promise an update cadence.

items.q: Will an update overwrite my MASTER.md?
items.a: --persist writes design-system/<project-slug>/MASTER.md under --output-dir (the current directory by default). Existing MASTER.md is preserved unless --force is used. Ask your assistant to read this file and the relevant page override; saving a file does not guarantee that every assistant loads it automatically.

items.q: How do I downgrade if a new version regresses my output?
items.a: Check npm versions before selecting a package version. Install that exact ui-ux-pro-max-cli version, then refresh the chosen skill installation. Back up local edits and read that version’s help; GitHub tags and package versions are not interchangeable.

items.q: My AI assistant does not seem to be using the skill.
items.a: Three common causes: (1) the assistant was started before the skill was installed — restart it; (2) the wrong assistant target was used — check the Manual Install table for the folder that assistant watches; (3) the assistant's project root is not where you ran uipro init — make sure you are in the same directory.

items.q: uipro: command not found.
items.a: npm global bin is not on PATH. Run npm config get prefix to find the bin path and add it to PATH, or reinstall with npm install -g ui-ux-pro-max-cli. If you used sudo, see the next question.

items.q: I get EACCES permission errors when installing globally.
items.a: Avoid sudo npm install -g. Use a Node version manager like fnm or nvm so your node install lives under your user. This sidesteps the permission issue and makes future upgrades safer.

items.q: search.py crashes with a JSON decode error.
items.a: Record the command and full error. Check the package version and local asset edits before reinstalling; a JSON error alone does not prove a failed download.

items.q: The output references libraries my stack does not use.
items.a: In CLI 2.15.0, run stack search separately: python3 .claude/skills/ui-ux-pro-max/scripts/search.py "forms accessibility" --stack shadcn. The --design-system branch takes precedence over --stack; combining them does not apply a stack filter to generation. Give both outputs to the assistant.
